analysis: Reviewed SSDPrefixCache.swift base 657-1836: the donate paths, the per-donation floor (883-888), dedupe/in-flight claims, sidecar claims (1139-1247), stage/readWindowSidecars binding checks (1391-1397, 1635-1650), staging release paths (1719-1754) and eviction/retirement (1769-1836). The only change is retireIndexedEntries (base 1793-1802, head 1794-1800). It used to take removalLock once for the whole URL batch. It now calls SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.removeInSlices, which takes removalLock separately for each slice. Each slice rechecks hasSafeRoot and ownsEvictionRoot (cache not closed and epoch current) under the lock before calling SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove with the same root, index and epochStore bindings. For T-041, the per-slice recheck keeps the fail-closed ownership guard. If the cache closes partway through, only the remaining slices are skipped, so expired ciphertext stays on disk until a later sweep. That is no worse than the base behavior, which skipped the whole batch when closed. The KEK purge, HMAC naming, AAD and TTL policy are untouched. evictOldestEntry passes one URL, so its behavior is effectively unchanged. Releasing the lock between slices may let concurrent indexed removals, reconciliation or forgetMissing interleave. Each operation still holds the lock individually, so no confidentiality impact is visible. Open integration questions: removeInSlices is not in the supplied source. Confirm that it (a) stops or skips safely on a nil slice result, (b) merges removed sets, indexedBytesFreed and externalChange across slices, and (c) uses a bounded slice size. Also confirm that callers of retireOwnedEntries (the TTL sweeper in SSDEvictableStore) tolerate partial results. No regression identified from the visible evidence.
